scope: Targeted primary-literature check for a design-and-simulation case study; not a systematic review or exhaustive novelty search.
method: Inspected primary publisher records and available author/institution-hosted papers through web retrieval. Search snippets alone were not used to support detailed method claims. No manuscript was uploaded to an external service.

sources.title: A Critical Look at Coulomb Counting Approach for State of Charge Estimation in Batteries
sources.inspection: Publisher citation record and NASA-hosted accepted manuscript, including abstract, inspected. NASA identifies the manuscript as externally peer reviewed and records publication on 6 July 2021. Later PDF section requests intermittently returned retrieval errors.
sources.supported_claim: Coulomb-counting errors can arise from current measurement, numerical integration, capacity uncertainty and timing; their accumulation requires attention to calibration and initialization.
sources.use_in_manuscript: Motivate the current/calibration and known-capacity limitations, while citing the established method rather than claiming it is new.
sources.limitation: Does not validate Wattsense, its sensor settings, its full-charge procedure, or any particular percentage SOC accuracy. The arXiv precursor has a different title and author-name variant; use the final journal metadata above.

sources.title: Priority-based low voltage DC microgrid system for rural electrification
sources.inspection: Publisher abstract and citation metadata retrieved. Direct publisher open failed, so the author-uploaded full paper (Ashish Shrestha, uploaded 20 November 2020) was inspected, especially section 2.2.2 and Table 3. Author byline matches the article title page.
sources.supported_claim: Earlier work combines SCADA with priority-based control in a DC microgrid, including three load levels and battery-charge thresholds for staged disconnection.
sources.use_in_manuscript: Closest practical prior art; establishes that maintaining essential-load service through lower-priority shedding is an existing concept.
sources.limitation: Its multi-level solar/microgrid experiment is not directly comparable to the two-load Wattsense discharge scenario. Its claimed reliability results must not be transferred to Wattsense.

sources.title: Enhanced demand side management for solar-based isolated microgrid system: Load prioritisation and energy optimisation
sources.inspection: Publisher full text inspected: abstract, sections 2.1-2.2, author metadata, and issue citation. First online 18 December 2023; cite the June 2024 volume/issue publication year.
sources.supported_claim: Priority-based demand management has also been formulated using day-ahead generation/load forecasts and particle-swarm optimization to allocate energy across load groups.
sources.use_in_manuscript: Position Wattsense as a local deterministic threshold case study with no forecasting or optimization; the difference is scope and implementation, not demonstrated superiority.
sources.limitation: No head-to-head comparison has been conducted. Do not quote its load-satisfaction or continuity percentages as evidence of Wattsense performance.

sources.title: Online estimation of battery equivalent circuit model parameters and state of charge using decoupled least squares technique
sources.inspection: University repository published-version PDF inspected: title page, abstract, introduction, experimental section 4.1 and discussion 6.1. Names follow the article byline; repository expands Dinh and Ascencio differently.
sources.supported_claim: Battery equivalent-circuit parameters depend on operating conditions; this study estimates fast and slow dynamics separately and tests the method with lithium-ion cell measurements.
sources.use_in_manuscript: Explain why Wattsense's assumed OCV/resistance plant is only a design-screening model and requires pack-specific characterization before predictive accuracy claims.
sources.limitation: The published experimental accuracy and cell parameters do not apply to the unmeasured Wattsense LiFePO4 pack; no DWRLS estimator is implemented in Wattsense.

synthesis: The established components are Coulomb counting, priority shedding, telemetry and equivalent-circuit modeling. A defensible contribution is reproducible integration of firmware checks, PCB-path assumptions and explicit service/startup tradeoffs. No novel control algorithm or hardware validation is established.
copyright_handling: All claims above are short original paraphrases. Do not copy external figures. Use original project diagrams and cite prior concepts. Keep the final paper's source-derived discussion concise; retrieval sources carried 200-word per-source response budgets.
